### Finite operating points

At \(\gamma/\Omega=2/\pi\), we have \(\mu=2\) and \(u^2\approx0.615168\,\eta<1\). All filter amplitudes and coupling strengths remain finite.

| Collection \(\eta\) | Detector efficiency \(\zeta\) | \(\gamma/\Omega\) | Guaranteed success probability | Conditional trace-distance error |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| \(1\) | \(1\) | \(2/\pi\) | \(0.204860639\) | Exactly \(0\) |
| \(0.999\) | \(0.999\) | \(2/\pi\) | \(>0.204\) | \(<0.007\) |
| \(0.25\) | No detector | \(10^{-3}\) | \(\ge2.325\times10^{-7}\) | \(\le0.0075\) |

The first row follows because every erroneous residual photon is detected. The second includes both inaccessible collection loss and detector inefficiency. Its conservative constants were verified with exact rational inequalities.

More generally, without a detector, the same construction gives

\[
p_{\checkmark}\ge
3.72\,\eta^2\left(\frac{\gamma}{\Omega}\right)^2,
\qquad
\text{conditional error}\le
7.5\,\frac{\gamma}{\Omega},
\]

for \(0<\gamma/\Omega\le10^{-3}\) and every \(0<\eta\le1\).

The poor success probability in the third row is a real limitation. **A failed attempt can consume the unknown input; repeating the experiment cannot recover that same state.**

I also executed the full cascaded-generator calculation, including loss and the no-click conditioning. At \(\eta=\zeta=0.999\), it gives success probability \(0.20508697\) and conditional Choi-state entanglement fidelity \(0.99832006\), consistent with the uniform analytic bound. The numerical check is independent corroboration, not the proof of the worst-input guarantee.

The derivation’s constants and full-generator checks are reproducible in [:chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"}](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_5abae267f32c819191d99df48292dd54&account_id=personal).

# Selected opening: a quantum state interface built from a fixed measurement port

**Can a fixed quantum measurement port be turned into a practical interface that exports an arbitrary unknown state—including its entanglement with an inaccessible reference—using a small causal receiver, without retaining or measuring the original carrier?**

The full destination is to make a class of quantum devices usable as sources of **quantum data**, through couplings otherwise used for readout. If this can be achieved at competitive fidelity, success probability and hardware cost, it could widen which processors, memories and simulators can be combined into large quantum machines.

I can substantiate a specific opening: **two receiving qubits, local filters and an output photon counter implement heralded state transfer through a continuously driven longitudinal measurement port.** In the stated Markov model, the transfer is exact with approximately **20.49% success** at perfect collection and detection. At collection and detector efficiencies of \(99.9\%\), a finite analytic bound guarantees **success above \(20.4\%\)** and **conditional trace-distance error below \(0.007\)**, uniformly over all input states and external references.

These are mathematical guarantees under explicit physical premises. The unresolved task is to obtain a competitive operating point in a finite-bandwidth device. The underlying connection between coherent measurements and state transfer is established prior work; the developed step here is a concrete receiver and an accounting of inaccessible photons.
